bull_bear.body: Board approved QIP up to Rs.500cr (primarily for working capital to support rapid growth and inventory needs); final size and utilization under review. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but focus on reinvestment for growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Working Capital Strain: Inventory days elevated to ~2.5 months due to logistics delays and new product stocking. Regulatory: BIS certification delays for inner groove tubes impacting imports. Geopolitical: Freight cost volatility and dispatch delays to UAE. Execution: Ramp-up speed of 8 new product lines.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident on long-term structural growth (Data Center, Bus AC); transparent about short-term working capital inefficiencies; aggressive on market share capture (15% in Bus AC); cautious on precise near-term numbers due to ramp-up variables.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The inventory buildup is largely strategic (BIS hedging) and logistical (UAE dispatch delay) rather than demand weakness; Rs.8cr of March exports are already shipped but unbilled, artificially inflating inventory and depressing Q4 revenue recognition. The company is effectively a 'hidden' liquid cooling play via its development of plate heat exchangers for CDUs.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Shareholding as of 30-06-2026: Promoter & Promoter Group 65.69%, Institutions 17.19%, Non-Institutions 17.13%.
- Equity share capital rose from ₹46.14 Cr (FY24) to ₹62.16 Cr (FY25 and FY26), consistent with the October-2024 NSE/BSE listing and capital raise.
- Current borrowings increased sharply from ₹32.04 Cr (FY25) to ₹187.10 Cr (FY26), while FY26 operating cash flow was negative (-₹113.80 Cr); growth has been funded mainly via financing activities (+₹147.69 Cr in FY26) rather than internal accruals.
- Reserves and Surplus grew from ₹84.15 Cr (FY24) to ₹511.84 Cr (FY26), largely reflecting listing-related capital and retained earnings.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Data Center: 16% of FY26 revenue, targeting 19% in FY27; key clients Schneider Electric, Vertiv (approval complete). Bus AC: Rs.10cr in FY26, targeting Rs.150cr. New Products: WOT, Roll-bond, Bar & Plate (Railways approved for trial), Dry Air Coolers. Exports: US, Europe, UAE.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for efficient thermal management in AI-driven data centers | KRN Heat Exchanger | beneficiary | High | Direct supplier to Schneider/Vertiv; expanding into liquid cooling components; 19% revenue share target. |
| Transition to electric buses and need for localized AC systems | KRN Heat Exchanger | beneficiary | High | High backward integration; targeting 15% market share; Rs.150cr revenue target. |
| Supply chain diversification away from China | KRN Heat Exchanger | beneficiary | Med | Exports doubling; competing with European/US suppliers rather than Chinese mass producers. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Positions itself as one of India's leading manufacturers of heat exchangers and HVAC&R solutions for residential, commercial and industrial applications, with a diversified portfolio spanning Fin & Tube Coils, Bar & Plate, Complete HVAC Systems, Bus AC Systems, Refrigeration Components, Technical Tubes, Sheet Metal Parts and Tubings.
- Serves diverse end-use industries: HVAC, refrigeration, data centers, automotive, railways, industrial cooling, process applications, power and marine.
- Established international footprint across roughly 19 countries (UAE, USA, Italy, Canada, France, UK, Germany and others in Europe, plus Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Nepal, China, Brazil); CMD notes products reached customers in 14 countries during Q1 FY27.
- Export share of the revenue mix has risen steadily: 14.68% (FY24) to 15.69% (FY25) to 16.57% (FY26).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Listing] Converted from a private to a public limited company and listed on NSE and BSE in October 2024.
- [Leadership] Founder-Chairman & Managing Director Mr. Santosh Kumar Yadav previously worked at Lloyd Electric & Engineering Limited before establishing KRN in 2017; holds a Diploma in Mechanical Engineering and a Diploma in Business Management (IMT Ghaziabad).
- [Board] Board comprises four Independent Directors (including a Cost Accountant/Company Secretary/Insolvency Professional and two Chartered Accountants) alongside the CMD, a Non-Executive Director and a Whole-Time Director.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Raw material pass-through: 100% of Copper/Aluminum LME and USD-INR fluctuations passed on quarterly. Margin drivers: PLI incentive (5%), RIFS state incentive (1.56% of revenue for 10 years), solar power savings. Headwinds: High depreciation and overheads from new facility ramp-up.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY27 New Facility Utilization: 50% (Targeting 80% in FY28); Export Revenue: ~2x YoY (from Rs.100cr); Bus AC Revenue Target: Rs.150cr (15% market share); Data Center Revenue Share: ~19% in FY27 (up from 16%); Margins: Expected expansion via PLI (5%), RIFS (1.56% of top-line), and solar savings.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Export order book ~Rs.120cr (includes Data Center); Bus AC secured 2-3 OEMs with regular supply; Data Center orders have 6-7 month lead times; Rolling orders from domestic HVAC majors.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Railway AC systems (6-8 month approval timeline); Liquid Cooling (CDU/Plate heat exchangers) for AI Data Centers (R&D ongoing, launch expected next year); Micro-channel heat exchangers (MCHX) portfolio addition by year-end.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: KRN Heat is transitioning from a pure-play fin-and-tube supplier to an integrated thermal solutions provider, driven by a newly commissioned 6x capacity facility and high-growth segments like Data Centers and Bus AC. While Q4FY26 showed strong top-line growth (Consolidated Revenue +33.5% YoY), inventory buildup due to export logistics and new product ramp-up temporarily suppressed cash flows, setting the stage for significant operating leverage in FY27 as utilization targets 50%.

open.item: Vertiv vendor code opened and QMS audit passed first-go; drawings under preparation, proto and mass production to start in coming weeks/months
Inventory up ~3x YoY (UAE ~Rs.15-20cr undispatched, Rs.8cr dispatched-unbilled, new-product minimum stock, BIS-driven import build); normalisation expected to take at least ~6 months, QoQ improvement
Plan to open 20-25 PAN-India bus-AC service centers within next 6-7 months (4 already opened: Indore, Noida, Delhi, Ahmedabad); hiring 50+ service technicians and 10-15 sales team
Achieved ~Rs.10 crore from bus AC in FY26; targeting ~15% market share (~Rs.150 crore per presentation) in FY27, backed by 2-3 OEMs already cracked with regular supply started
Developing micro-channel (MCHX) heat exchanger to be added to portfolio by end of this year or early next year; also studying plate/CDU heat exchangers for liquid cooling to potentially add next year

Approved by Indian Railways for bar-and-plate heat exchanger (post 6-month field trial completed Feb); L1 in three tenders last week, orders expected this week; full HVAC-system railway entry needs ~6-8 more months
Expect 5% PLI benefit this year on heat-exchanger production and RIPS approval possibly within the month (~1.56% of top line for new facility for 10 years)
Plan to roughly double export revenue in FY27 vs ~Rs.100 crore achieved in FY26, across North America, Europe and UAE
Expect ~50% capacity utilisation from the new HVAC facility in FY27 (across all products and geometries), with old KRN Heat facility already fully utilised
Currently four independent directors (finance and CS expertise); plan to add 1-3 more industry-expert independent directors, visible on Board next year
Expect ~10-15% growth on existing railway/metro heat exchanger business (small share of total)
Management expects next eight quarters to be highest-ever, with much faster QoQ capacity ramp than prior 2-3 quarters as new products clear customer/railway approvals
Roughly Rs.30-40 crore capex planned on the existing facility over the next two years for line balancing / data-center geometry (main 6x CAPEX largely done)
Expect slight margin improvement from PLI, RIPS, higher exports and solar savings, partly offset by high depreciation and rising overhead; recent copper/aluminium spike a near-term drag
New facility utilisation to reach ~80% in FY28 (next year after the 50% FY27 target)
Target to achieve at least 50% export share from existing products within 3 years (from ~16-18% now)
Analyst-referenced peak revenue target of Rs.2,250-2,850 crore (FY28/FY29); management would not confirm the revenue number but reaffirmed 50%/80% utilisation path
Board approved enabling QIP of up to Rs.500 crore (may not use full amount), mainly for working capital; objective not yet concluded
Post-tariff, expect to offer 15-20% lower landed price vs European/US suppliers; Thermotech lab enabling 7mm-to-5mm tube redesign saving ~10% on same capacity
Bus air-conditioning gross margin better than existing product, above 20%, due to complete assembly and backward integration
